the effects of short-range correlations are important at large emission angles and the effects of mesonic currents are important at small emission angles.

the nucleon knockout reaction is a very sensitive tool to investigate the short range correlation effects in the nuclear wave function, and that the effects of the meson exchange current are even more important.

the study of short-range correlations and meson exchange effects in photonucleon emission processes.
the study of the role of short-range correlations and meson exchange current effects on one-nucleon emission in photonucleon reactions.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of short-range correlations and meson exchange current are of the same order of magnitude, but they are of different sign.

the nucleon knockout model is not a good approximation at all energies and momentum transfers, and that it is necessary to include meson exchange currents and short-range correlation effects in order to describe the nucleon emission process.

, at least for the one-nucleon emission cross sections, the direct knock-out mechanism is a good approximation for photon energies above the giant dipole resonance region and momentum transfers up to 1.5 fm−1, but the presence of meson exchange and short-range correlation effects cannot be neglected.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nucleon emission process is very complicated and the theoretical predictions are rather sensitive to the model assumptions.
the direct knock-out mechanism is a good description for nucleon emission in the region above the giant resonance.

the nucleon knock-out process at large nucleon emission angles is dominated by the effects of mesonic corrections and the short-range correlation effects can be safely neglected in the description of the nucleon emission cross section.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a proper treatment of short-range correlations and meson exchange current effects is crucial for the description of the photo-emission process.
the effects of short-range correlations are not negligible in the description of nucleon photo-emissions, but that their role is not so important as the effects of mesonic currents.
